changed: Dances you import from The Caller's Box read a neighbor number before the men or the women as a figure instead of text. When only the men or only the women take part, it names them among those neighbors: "N2 Men allemande left 3/4" is the next larks (in your dialect's words) allemanding, and "N0 Women" are the previous robins. When the figure is done with a neighbor, the number names the neighbor: "N2 Men roll away neighbor" has the larks roll away their next neighbors. Otherwise, such as "N3 Men allemande" or a figure done with partners, the number is kept as a note. A figure that ends in the number instead, such as "Men allemande left 3/4 [with N2]", reads the same way.

Dances you import from The Caller's Box read a hey whose passes name same-role neighbors (SRN) as a hey, and keep "with hands" or a trailing "[with N1]" on a hey as a note instead of leaving the line as text.
Dances you import from The Caller's Box read "Pass the ocean (to wave of four (NR,WL))" as a pass the ocean into that wave.

The Caller's Box figure dialect reads a neighbour number before a role pair (`N2 role1s …`) as the role among those neighbours (`nextRole1s`, `prevRole2s`) when only that role takes part, as the numbered neighbours in `whom` or `who2` when the figure is done with a neighbour, and otherwise as the role pair with a `with` note; a role-pair clause ending in a lone `[with N0]`–`[with N4]` reads the same way. It also decodes `SRN` (same-role neighbours) in hey pass lists and keeps `with hands` and a trailing `[with …]` as the hey's note, and reads a nested wave annotation on pass the ocean.
